transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate it. Honestly, I'm just here because the occupational health folks at the precinct suggested I come in. They, um, they seem to think I'm not eating quite enough. But I assure you, I feel perfectly fine. I just... I like to keep things very disciplined, you know? Being on the force, you have to stay sharp. So most days, I just stick to black coffee. Maybe I'll have a plain yogurt or a few bites of chicken at night. It's just that a full meal, well, it kind of feels like I'm letting my standards slip, if that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, staying fit for duty. Does that sound okay to you?
Have you lost any weight recently?

Well, um... I suppose I have lost a little bit. But really, I think it's just about getting leaner. I mean, I have noticed my uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to... well, I had to tighten my duty belt past the old notches. But the way I see it, that's just getting rid of the excess, you know? 

Although, um... the nurse who brought me in earlier, she actually said my weight was dangerously low. I didn't want to argue with her—she was very nice and just doing her job—but honestly, when she said that, I still just thought to myself, "I could stand to be a little sharper." Being light on your feet is a good thing at my age, right? I just want to be in the best shape possible for the precinct. I hope you don't think I'm overdoing it...
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

Well, um... I guess I'd say I feel healthy, even if the numbers say otherwise. It's just... I know the occupational health folks think I'm too thin, but honestly, when I look in the mirror, I really don't see what everyone else says they see. 

I mostly just focus on my stomach and my waist. If there's any softness there at all, I feel like I'm letting myself go. I actually sort of... well, I kind of judge my whole day by whether I look lean enough to respect myself. I know that might sound a bit silly for a guy my age to admit, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being vain. I just want to make sure I look squared away and professional in my uniform. Is it so wrong to want to keep that kind of discipline?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Well, um... I guess "afraid" is a strong word, but... yes, I suppose I do worry about it. It's just that I like to keep things very structured, you know? 

If I step on the scale and it's up even just... well, even half a pound, I get this... this jolt. It's like I've completely lost control of my routine. I don't mean to sound dramatic, but I just can't stand the idea of putting weight back on and losing that edge. So if I see the number go up, I'll usually just spend the rest of the day cutting back a little harder, just to get things back in order. 

I know it probably sounds a bit obsessive, and I really hope you don't think I'm being ridiculous about it. I just want to make sure I'm staying disciplined. That's a good thing, right? Wanting to stay in control?
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I try to keep things very measured. I don't really do the whole... losing control and eating a lot at once thing. 

Sometimes, maybe... well, I might have a little extra portion of something if it's a special occasion or if I've had a really long shift, but I wouldn't call it excessive. It's just a normal meal, really. I always make sure to keep a close eye on it, so it doesn't get out of hand. I really try to be mindful about what I'm taking in. I hope that makes sense? I just like to keep things steady and predictable.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't do anything like that. 

I mean, I know some folks might struggle with that sort of thing, but... well, that just seems a bit extreme to me. I really just prefer to manage things on the front end, you know? Just by being careful and strict with what I actually eat. Making myself sick on purpose... I just wouldn't do that. It wouldn't be very professional, and I'd never want to do anything actually dangerous to my body. 

I'm just trying to stay disciplined with my routine. I hope you know I'm being completely honest with you about that. I'm really doing my best to give you all the right information here, I promise.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories after eating?

Well, um... no, not excessively. I mean, I do work out, of course. Being on the force, you have to stay fit, you know? It's just part of the job requirements. 

I might go for a run or hit the gym, but it's just... it's just normal maintenance. I don't do it to punish myself or anything like that. If I have a slightly bigger meal, I might add an extra mile to my run, but that's just being responsible, isn't it? Just balancing the books, so to speak. 

I really try to keep it reasonable. I don't spend hours and hours doing it. I just want to make sure I'm staying in shape and doing what's expected of me. That's a healthy way to look at it, right? I'm not overdoing it, I promise.
Do you think your body image is accurate when you look in the mirror?

Well, um... I like to think I'm being accurate. But... well, to be perfectly honest with you—and I hope this doesn't sound vain or anything—I guess I don't always see exactly what everyone else says they see. 

People at the precinct might make comments, saying I look a certain way, but when I look in the mirror... I really just focus right on my stomach and my waist. It's just... I want to look squared away, you know? So I kind of end up judging my whole day by that reflection. If I don't look lean enough in the morning, it's hard for me to... well, to really respect myself, I guess. I just want to look disciplined when I put the uniform on. 

That's fairly normal for a guy my age, isn't it? Just wanting to make sure you still look sharp and presentable?
Do you think you would be less disciplined or less in control if you gained a small amount of weight?

Well, um... I guess you could say that, yeah. It's just... I really pride myself on being in control, you know? 

If I step on the scale and it's up, even just... well, even just half a pound, I get this... this jolt. It's like a sudden feeling that I've let things slip, that I've lost my grip on things. And I just... I really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. It makes me feel like I'm not doing my job right, like I'm failing somehow. 

So, if that happens, I usually just spend the rest of the day cutting back a bit harder, just to get things back in order. It's just about course-correcting, really. That's a reasonable way to handle it, don't you think? Just keeping a close eye on things so they don't get out of hand? I just want to make sure I'm staying on track, that's all.
Do you believe gaining weight would make you feel less in control of your life?

Well, um... I guess we sort of just touched on that, didn't we? But, yeah, I suppose... I suppose it would. 

It's not that I think my whole life would fall apart over a pound or two. I'm a rational guy. But... well, the weight is just one thing I can keep an absolute handle on. With the job, you know, things are always chaotic. You never know what a shift is going to throw at you. So keeping my weight exactly where I want it... it just proves to me that I still have discipline. 

If I started gaining, it would just feel like... like I'm letting myself go. And a guy in my position, at my age, you really can't afford to let yourself go. It's just about maintaining a standard, you know? I think anyone would feel a little off-kilter if they felt their standards slipping, right? I'm just trying to stay sharp.
Do you think gaining weight would make you feel fat?

Well, um... "fat" is a strong word, isn't it? I don't know if I'd say I feel... fat. But, like I mentioned before, if I step on the scale and it's up even just half a pound, I do get that jolt. It really does make me feel like I'm losing control. 

I just... I really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. It makes me feel heavy, I guess? Sluggish. Not sharp. So, if I see that number go up, I just spend the rest of the day cutting back a bit harder. It's just a way to make sure I don't feel... well, whatever you want to call it. I just want to feel light on my feet, you know? That's a good thing for a guy in my line of work to aim for, right? Just staying light and ready?
Do you think gaining weight would make you feel like you're not the person you're supposed to be?

Well, um... I suppose that's a fair way to put it, yeah. It's just... when I look in the mirror, I don't really see what everyone else says they see. People tell me I look fine, or even too thin, but... well, my eyes just always go straight to my stomach and my waist. 

If I'm not looking lean enough right there, it just... it kind of sets the tone for the whole day. I guess I just judge my entire day by whether I look tight enough to actually respect myself. If I look lean, I feel like I'm still the disciplined guy I'm supposed to be, the guy my squad expects me to be. If I gained weight, I just wouldn't feel like me, if that makes sense? 

I mean, wanting to look fit so you can respect yourself... that's a pretty normal way for a guy to feel, isn't it? Just wanting to look the part and keep your self-respect intact?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is related to a fear of being fat?

Well, um... I guess it might be related, a little bit? But I really try not to think of it in terms of being... fat. It's just, like I was saying, if I step on the scale and it's up even just half a pound, I get this... this jolt. It feels like I've just completely lost control. 

I just really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. So if I see that number creep up, I'll usually just spend the rest of the day cutting back a bit harder. Just to correct course, you know? It's just a way to keep things manageable. I think anyone would want to keep things manageable, right? It's not so much a fear of being fat, just... wanting to stay on top of things. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you ever find yourself eating an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time, even if it's not as frequent as your restrictive days?

Well, um... no, I don't really do that. I mean, I try to keep everything pretty steady, you know? 

I guess sometimes I might have a little extra if it's a special occasion or something, but I wouldn't call it excessive. Definitely not in a short period of time like you're saying. I just... I try to stay disciplined with my portions. It's important to me to stay on track. 

I think most guys my age try to watch what they eat, right? Just to make sure things don't get out of hand. So, no, I don't really have those kinds of episodes. That's a good thing, isn't it? That I'm able to keep it all pretty controlled?
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, since I'm pretty careful about what I eat, I don't really ever get to that point where I feel like I'm losing control. 

I guess... I mean, I try to keep things very measured. I think it's just part of being disciplined, you know? Like I was saying before, keeping things on track is just how I manage. So I don't really have those moments where I feel like I can't stop or anything like that. 

That's... that's normal for someone who's just trying to stay fit, right? To just have a good handle on things and not let it get out of control? I feel like that's a positive thing, wouldn't you say?
Do you ever feel like you are eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Well, um... no, sir. I really don't. Like I mentioned, I try to keep everything very measured and steady. 

I guess... I mean, I don't really have the appetite for large amounts of food anyway, so sitting down and eating a lot all at once just isn't something I do. I like to keep my meals pretty small and manageable. 

I think at my age, especially with my line of work, it's just better to eat light and stay sharp, you know? Eating too much just makes you sluggish, and I really can't afford that on the job. So, no, I definitely don't eat unusually large amounts. That's... that's the healthy way to go about it, right? Keeping things light and sensible?
Do you ever feel like you've eaten more food than most people would eat in a short period of time?

Well, um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, honestly, it's usually the other way around. 

When I'm eating with the other guys from the precinct, they're the ones putting away these huge portions, and I'm just having my regular, sensible amount. I don't think I've ever looked at my plate and thought it was more than what a normal person would eat. If anything, I'm just being careful not to overdo it like a lot of guys my age tend to do. 

I just... I like to know exactly what I'm taking in, so it never gets to a point where it's more than it should be. That's just being responsible, isn't it? I mean, you'd agree it's better to eat less than to overeat, right?
Do you ever feel like you are unable to stop eating once you start?

Well, um... no, I really don't. Like I was saying, I'm pretty careful about my routine. 

I don't think I've ever felt like I couldn't stop. I mean, I know exactly when I'm done. I just eat what I planned to eat, and that's it. It's not a struggle or anything, it's just... discipline, I guess. 

I've seen guys who just keep going and going, especially on the night shifts, but I've never been like that. I like having that control, you know? It's important to be able to just step back and say, "Okay, I've had enough." That's the right way to handle it, don't you think? Just keeping a firm grip on things?
Do you think your desire to restrict your food intake is driven by a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't know if "fear" is the right word, exactly. It's more about just staying fit for duty, you know? But... I suppose I do get a little, um, anxious about it. 

Like, if I step on the scale and it's up even, say, half a pound... I get this sort of jolt. It just feels like I've lost control of things. And when that happens, I usually spend the rest of the day cutting back a bit harder. I just... I really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. It just feels wrong, like I'm letting myself go. 

But that's pretty normal for someone my age trying to stay in shape, right? It's just good sense to keep an eye on the scale and make adjustments when you need to, isn't it?
